Translate a registry layer style to a QGIS QML document

Source: R/gq_qgis_style.R
gq_qgis_style.Rd

Builds the QGIS-native form of a registry layer's symbology, so a layer defined only in a custom registry CSV (gq_reg_custom()) can be handed to QGIS coloured as gq_tmap_style() and gq_mapgl_style() draw it. A classified line or polygon becomes a categorized renderer with one category per class; an unclassified one becomes a single-symbol renderer.

Usage

gq_qgis_style(layer_or_reg, name = NULL, field = NULL, path = NULL)

Arguments

layer_or_reg

Either a layer entry from the registry (e.g., reg$layers$lake) or a full registry list when using name-based lookup.

name

Optional layer name for name-based lookup. Accepts name_qgis_snake (e.g., "lake") or name_qgis (e.g., "Crossings - PSCIS assessment"). Normalized to match registry keys.

field

Optional character string to override the classification field name. Useful when data comes from an alternative source with a different column name (e.g., bcfishpass barrier_status vs WHSE barrier_result_code). inst/registry/xref_layers.csv lists the known alternatives: for each layer key, the database table the bundled data was queried from (name_table, e.g. bcfishpass.crossings) and the column that table classifies on (class_field).

path

Optional file path. When given, the QML is also written there (UTF-8), and returned invisibly.

Value

A length-one character string holding the QML document. Put it in a .qml file beside a layer, or into a GeoPackage's layer_styles table with gq_gpkg_style_write().

Details

For a layer gq ships a QML for, prefer gq_style_qml(): that file is what QGIS itself wrote, and carries what the registry does not model (labels, multi-layer symbols, casing, scale-dependent rendering). This function writes only what the registry holds.

What each registry property becomes:

  • class value and label: a <category>'s value and label;

  • colour: QGIS's r,g,b,a form, from hex or an R colour name;

  • line width and polygon outline width: millimetres, as the registry holds them (QGIS's default of 0.26 mm where the registry gives none);

  • line dash: a named QGIS line_style (dash, dot, dash dot, ...) or, for a pattern such as "4;2", a custom dash;

  • line opacity: the symbol's alpha; polygon fill and outline opacity: the alpha of each colour (to the nearest 1/255), so the two can differ as the registry allows;

  • a polygon class's outline: its own outline_color and outline_width when the registry has them, else the layer's stroke, else no outline.

Not written: labels, a line's overlay (a warning says so), and point and raster layers, which error. An unclassified layer the registry gives no fill or stroke colour (one whose QGIS symbol it could not model) errors too.

See also

gq_gpkg_style_write() to store it in a GeoPackage, gq_style_qml() for the QML files gq ships.

Examples

reg <- gq_reg_custom(system.file("registry", "reg_custom.csv", package = "gq"))

# a classified line: one category per class
qml <- gq_qgis_style(reg, "habitat_rule_comparison")
doc <- xml2::read_xml(qml)
cats <- xml2::xml_find_all(doc, ".//categories/category")
data.frame(
  value = xml2::xml_attr(cats, "value"),
  label = xml2::xml_attr(cats, "label")
)
#>     value                       label
#> 1    both                  Both rules
#> 2   first             First rule only
#> 3  second            Second rule only
#> 4 outside Floodplain outside the rule
# each class's colour, in QGIS's r,g,b,a form
xml2::xml_attr(
  xml2::xml_find_all(doc, ".//symbols/symbol//Option[@name='line_color']"),
  "value"
)
#> [1] "27,108,168,255" "217,95,2,255"   "27,158,119,255" "123,63,152,255"

# an unclassified polygon: a single symbol
xml2::xml_attr(
  xml2::xml_find_first(xml2::read_xml(gq_qgis_style(reg, "rivers_poly")),
                       ".//renderer-v2"),
  "type"
)
#> [1] "singleSymbol"

# write it beside a layer
out <- tempfile(fileext = ".qml")
gq_qgis_style(reg, "bec_zone", path = out)
file.exists(out)
#> [1] TRUE
